claims.text: Conventional TOR-TILD EAM reference potentials inadequately represent the breadth of ab initio liquid configurations in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
This inadequate representation produces significant thermodynamic-integration path mismatches.
An ML interatomic potential can be trained on ab initio liquid and high-temperature solid configurations.
Gaussian Approximation Potentials or Moment Tensor Potentials are suitable example frameworks for the proposed reference potential.
High-temperature liquid states contain many short-lived and metastable local atomic configurations.
A suitably trained ML potential will capture a wider variety of these local configurations than a conventional EAM reference.
Training on ab initio configurations spanning the relevant solid and liquid phase space will allow the ML potential to mimic target interaction energies more accurately.
More accurate reproduction of target interaction energies will improve overlap between the ML-reference and ab initio target ensembles.
Improved reference–target ensemble overlap will produce a shorter and more reliable thermodynamic-integration path.
The ML reference will markedly reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
Free-energy estimates obtained with the ML reference will more closely match independent ab initio benchmarks.
Melting predictions obtained with the ML reference will more closely match experimental melting data.
The proposed intervention is applicable approximately from 0.9Tm to Tm.
The intervention is applicable to compositions whose configurational disorder makes conventional EAM potentials insufficient.
The degree of improvement depends on the quality and diversity of the ML training data.
Extreme chemical complexity or strongly nonequilibrium conditions may reduce the ML potential's efficacy and require refinement.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant path-mismatch reduction or closer agreement with benchmark free energies would falsify the hypothesis.
